title: fix(spec): five exported symbols resolved to `any` — type the recursive schemas and gate it in CI (#4171)
body:
Closes #4171.

## The mechanism

A recursive Zod schema needs an explicit annotation to break its circular inference, and five of them took the cheapest one available:

```ts
export const NavigationItemSchema: z.ZodType<any> = z.lazy(() => …);
export type NavigationItem = z.infer<typeof NavigationItemSchema>;   // → any
```

It compiles, it validates correctly at runtime, and it silently throws the type away. `NavigationItem`, `FormField`, `JoinNode` and `NormalizedFilter` were all `any` on the published surface — plus `FieldNodeSchema`, which had no exported type alias yet, so `z.infer<typeof FieldNodeSchema>` was `any` and `QueryAST['fields']` with it. It is one alias away from having been a fifth entry in the issue's table, and invisible to a types-only scan.

That is worse than a missing export. #4115 tells every consumer that a local declaration under a spec export's name must be replaced by a binding to the spec — and for these, obeying it **replaced a precise type with `any`**. The reason it survives review is that `any` agrees with everything, so the natural "are these the same type?" check answers yes in *both* directions and recommends precisely the wrong action. Same failure family as #4075's `[key: string]: any` on `ActionDef`.

## The fix

Annotate with the real type, using the pattern `QueryAST` already follows in `data/query.zod.ts` — infer the non-recursive part, tie the recursive knot in the type, so the keys stay derived from the schema rather than hand-maintained beside it:

```ts
const BaseXSchema = z.object({ …every non-recursive key });
export type X = z.infer<typeof BaseXSchema> & { children?: X[] };
export const XSchema: z.ZodType<X> = z.lazy(() => BaseXSchema.extend({
  children: z.array(XSchema).optional(),
}));
```

`z.infer` now resolves to what it should always have been: `NavigationItem` the nine-branch union, `FormField` the 30-key form-field contract (`visibleOn` absent by construction — ADR-0089 D2 folds it into `visibleWhen` at the boundary), `JoinNode` and the newly exported `FieldNode` the query AST nodes, `NormalizedFilter` the normalized filter AST. **Runtime validation is unchanged** — every schema parses exactly what it parsed before (7114 spec tests green, including the `.strict()` / error-map behaviour of the split-and-extended `FormFieldSchema`). Both new base schemas stay `lazySchema`-wrapped so splitting them out does not move construction back to module load.

## What the types immediately caught

None of it visible while they were `any`:

- **`account.app.ts` set `defaultOpen` on three nav groups** — a key the spec has never declared. It worked only because objectui's `NavigationRenderer` still falls back to that legacy alias (`expanded` wins, `defaultOpen` second). Fixed at the producer per Prime Directive #12, not by widening the schema: the canonical key is `expanded`.
- **The MongoDB driver keyed its projection on the node object.** `find()` did `projection[field] = 1` over `query.fields`, so a relationship `FieldNode` would have produced the projection key `"[object Object]"`. It now reads the node's field name (the nested select is resolved by the engine's expand path, never by the driver).
- **Authoring literals annotated with the PARSED type were omitting `.default()`ed keys** — `expanded` in `setup.app.ts` / `studio.app.ts`, `target` in `setup-nav.contributions.ts`, `span` on the form fields `metadata-protocol` synthesizes for `getUiView`. Each now states the default it was relying on, matching what those same literals already do for `active` / `isDefault` / `collapsible` / `collapsed` / `columns` (and what `group_advanced` already did for `expanded`).

## The gate

`packages/spec/scripts/check-exported-any.ts`, wired into the required **TypeScript Type Check** job next to `check:api-surface`.

`api-surface.json` records that an export *exists* and never what it *resolves to* — which is how these survived a whole major with every gate green. The new scan reads the built `.d.ts` a consumer's import actually resolves to and fails on:

1. any exported **type** that resolves to `any` — what the consumer binds to;
2. any exported **schema** whose output is `any` — the root cause, and `any` for anyone writing `z.infer<typeof XSchema>` even before a named type exists.

Scope is deliberately tight: the type must *be* `any`. `Record<string, any>`, `any[]`, an `$eq?: any` operator field are not flagged, so the gate stays at zero false positives and red keeps meaning broken.

`KNOWN_ANY` is the escape hatch, shrink-only — an entry that no longer resolves to `any` fails until it is deleted, so a fix cannot leave a stale exemption behind to cover the next regression. **It is currently empty**: all five were fixed rather than declared.

It runs `--self-test` first (the repo's `check:route-envelope` / `check:wildcard-fallthrough` convention), compiling a fixture against the real zod. For a check whose green result is "nothing found", the failure that matters most is going dormant — so the day zod renames the internals it reads (`_output`), it fails loudly instead of passing everything forever.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| spec test suite | 7114 passed (273 files) |
| `turbo run build --filter='./packages/*' --filter='./examples/*^...'` | 66/66 |
| `turbo run test --filter='./packages/*'` | green (one 30s timeout flake in `cloud-connection` under parallel load; that file and the whole package pass on re-run) |
| examples typecheck / downstream-contract typecheck | clean — the frozen third-party consumer still compiles against the narrowed types |
| spec gates | `check:docs` `check:api-surface` `check:exported-any` `check:authorable-surface` `check:spec-changes` `check:upgrade-guide` `check:skill-refs` `check:skill-docs` `check:react-blocks` `check:skill-examples` `check:liveness` `check:empty-state` `check:react-conformance` all PASS |
| root gates | `lint` `check:i18n` `check:i18n-coverage` `check:nul-bytes` `check:doc-authoring` `check:role-word` `check:org-identifier` `check:authz-resolver` `check:route-envelope` `check:error-code-casing` `check:wildcard-fallthrough` `check:release-notes` all PASS |
| gate negative-tested | restoring `z.ZodType<any>` on `NormalizedFilterSchema` → exit 1 naming it; a stale `KNOWN_ANY` entry → exit 1 |

Regenerated: `api-surface.json` (one addition, `FieldNode (type)` — no removals, no kind changes, factory signatures unchanged) and `content/docs/references/ui/view.mdx` (`fields` row moves, since `.extend()` appends it).

## Notes

- **No objectui change is needed on this PR.** objectui consumes the published `^17.0.0-rc.0`, so objectui#3042's deliberately inverted `true satisfies IsAny<…>` tripwires stay green until the release lands — at which point they fail and name the symbols whose ledger entries can be burned down, which is exactly their design.
- **Follow-up, filed separately:** `z.input` of these schemas is still `unknown` (`z.ZodType<Out>` leaves `Input` defaulted), so `AppInput['navigation']` is `unknown[]` and the authoring surface is unchecked. That is why the fix above spells the defaults out in the authoring artifacts instead of retyping them to the input surface — the honest fix needs precise input types first, and that is a wider change than this issue.
